changes.after: A bit mask lets one number hold several on-or-off flags.

before: An unsigned value can store flags in separate bit positions. 1u and 2u select different low bits.
flags | mask sets the bits in mask. flags & mask keeps only shared bits. Comparing that result with 0 asks whether a flag is present.
Unsigned bit operations avoid signed representation assumptions. Shifts still need a count smaller than the promoted type width; this example needs no shifts.
The |= operator updates flags with the bitwise OR result, preserving bits already set.
Expected output or behavior: 1. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Test each flag separately after setting only one. Distinguish logical && from a bitwise & mask. You may trace it without a C compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A bit holds 0 or 1. A flag uses one bit to mean off or on. The unsigned values `1u` and `2u` select two different bit positions. The u means unsigned.
A mask is a number whose set bits choose the positions you want. `flags | mask` turns those positions on. `flags & mask` keeps only positions that are on in both numbers.
Unsigned integers are useful for bit operations because they do not have a negative sign to handle. This example uses fixed masks, so no bit shifting is needed.
`flags |= 2u` turns on the bit selected by 2u and stores the result in flags. Bits that were already on stay on.
The update turns on the 2u bit. The `&` test finds that bit, and `!= 0u` turns the answer into true. printf displays 1.
Remove the update and look only for the 2u bit. Having the 1u bit on does not turn on the 2u bit.

before.question: Remove the flags |=2u statement. What does the flag test print?
choices: 1 because any nonzero flags includes every bit.
2 because the mask becomes the result.
before.explanation: The second bit is absent until it is set.

after.question: Remove `flags |= 2u;`. What does the test print?
choices: 1, because any nonzero number has every flag.
0, because the 2u flag is not set.
after.explanation: flags stays at 1u. Its bit does not overlap the 2u mask, so the test is false and prints 0.
